evaluated_conduct: The appellate admissibility disposition in ECCA v Commission concerning whether a first-instance intervener was directly affected within Article 56 of the Statute.

reasoning.statement: Article 56 requires the General Court decision itself to directly affect the intervener's own legal situation; first-instance intervention interest and effects on the supported main party are insufficient.
Because ECCA did not establish the required direct effect, the Court dismissed the appeal as inadmissible and did not adjudicate the substantive pesticide-regulatory grounds.

unresolved_questions: Any proposition about chlorpyrifos-methyl scientific risk, read-across, weight of evidence, or the substantive validity of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/17 requires separate merits-source analysis.

mizan.explanation: No Mizan result is generated from a procedural appellate inadmissibility judgment.
